summary: In 1911 a fire at the Triangle Waist Company factory in New York killed 146 mostly immigrant garment workers trapped behind locked doors; owners Max Blanck and Isaac Harris, who had violently fought a strike, were acquitted and profited from insurance.
keywords: Triangle: The Fire That Changed America

evidence.note: Harris and Blanck emigrate from Russia and settle in New York in the early 1890s
the two found the Triangle Waist Company in 1900
fall 1909 union drive and strike begin; owners fire union members
fire kills 146 within eighteen minutes in March 1911
Triangle company finally shuts down in 1918
owners hire pimps, prostitutes and police to break the strikers' blockade
owners set up a fake company union to divert organizing
repeated likely deliberate fires for insurance payouts; over-insured before 1911
